descriptions.text:
This course introduces students to anthropological linguistics, the interdisciplinary field that studies language as a culturally embedded, socially situated, and cognitively meaningful practice. It explores how linguistic structures, language use, and communicative practices are intertwined with cultural models, systems of classification, social relations, and ways of experiencing the world.
Starting from foundational debates on language, thought, and perception (linguistic relativity), the course examines how meaning is constructed, negotiated, and indexed across linguacultures. Through a range of empirical case studies, students engage with topics such as visual perception and the color debate, naming practices, gender, narrative and truth, language socialization, cultural keywords, and cultural conceptualizations of personhood, health, and illness.
While the course places a particular focus on Africa and South-East Asia, students are also introduced to case studies from across the world. This comparative perspective highlights the diversity of linguistic and cultural systems and challenges universalist assumptions about language and cognition.
The course combines theoretical readings with student-led ethnographic observations and class presentations, encouraging critical reflection on how language mediates cognition, social life, and cultural knowledge. Students are also introduced to key methodological approaches in anthropological linguistics, including the ethnography of communication. Questions of reflexivity, responsibility, and knowledge pluralism in research will also be discussed.
By the end of the course, students will have gained a solid understanding of key concepts and approaches in anthropological linguistics, as well as the analytical tools needed to critically examine language as a central component of human cultural life and as a means through which social meanings and relations are constructed and maintained.
Required readings for each week will be announced via Brightspace.

#### Assessment

* Weekly participation in close engagement with the required readings on the Discussion Board.
* A mini-assignment consisting of an ethnographic observation.
* A presentation in groups of two of a research article on one of the topics handled in class.
* A written exam based on the topics discussed in class.

#### Weighing

The final grade for this course is calculated as follows:

* Participation on the discussion board and ethnographic observation: 10%
* Class presentation and engagement in class discussion: 20%
* Final exam: 70%

**In order to participate in the final exam, participation on the discussion board and a class presentation are compulsory components**.

Enrolment through [MyStudyMap](https://mijn.universiteitleiden.nl/login) is mandatory.
General information about course and exam enrolment is available on the [website](https://www.student.universiteitleiden.nl/en/administrative-matters/registration--de-registration/course-and-exam-enrolment/course-and-exam-enrolment/humanities/art-history-ba?cf=humanities&cd=art-history-ba#tab-2).

#### Registration *À la carte education*, *Contract teaching* and *Exchange*

* Information for those interested in taking this course in context of [À la carte education ](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/education/other-modes-of-study/contract-and-non-examination-courses/a-la-carte-education)(without taking examinations), eg. about costs, registration and conditions.
* Information for those interested in taking this course in context of [Contract teaching](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/education/other-modes-of-study/contract-and-non-examination-courses/contract-teaching) (with taking examinations), eg. about costs, registration and conditions.
* For the registration of exchange students contact [Humanities International Office](mailto:exchange@hum.leidenuniv.nl).

Students from outside the BA Linguistics and BA African Studies are welcome to join too. If MyStudymap indicates the course is full, please contact the[ education coordinator](mailto:stucoafrican@hum.leidenuniv.nl). If a larger room cannot be found, priority will be given to students from the BA Linguistics and BA African Studies.

* For substantive questions, contact the lecturer listed in the right information bar.
* For questions about enrollment, admission, etc, contact the Education Administration Office: [Reuvensplaats](mailto:osz-oa-reuvensplaats@hum.leidenuniv.nl)
Participation and presentations are obligatory in order to do the final exam.
The timetables are available through My Timetable (see the button in the upper right corner).

Resit of final exam. 

#### Inspection and feedback

How and when an exam review will take place will be disclosed together with the publication of the exam results at the latest. If a student requests a review within 30 days after publication of the exam results, an exam review will have to be organized.

descriptions.value: Acquiring knowledge by systematically and methodically inquiring into a situation or concept, making use of methods appropriate to the academic field or discipline.
Kennis verwerven door het systematisch en methodisch bevragen van een situatie of concept waarbij gebruik gemaakt wordt van methoden die passen bij het vakgebied of de discipline.
Analysing situations or information and deciding what is of major and lesser importance. Seeing interrelationships and getting to the core of the matter.
Ontleden van situaties of een hoeveelheid informatie in hoofd- en bijzaken. Zien van onderlinge verbanden en doordringen tot de kern.
Making ideas and information clear to others through spoken words, using comprehensible language and checking that the message has been understood.
Ideeën en informatie in begrijpelijke gesproken taal aan anderen duidelijk maken en nagaan of de boodschap begrepen is.
Conveying ideas and information clearly to an audience, taking account of the target group and using appropriate supporting materials and platforms.
Ideeën en informatie op heldere wijze overbrengen aan een publiek, rekening houdend met de doelgroep. Hierbij worden passende ondersteunende materialen en platformen gebruikt.
Self-directing own process of absorbing and applying new knowledge and information.
Zelf sturing geven aan het eigen proces van nieuwe kennis en informatie opnemen en toepassen.
